groups.defect: The async legacy-write goroutines get their context from the request ctx through context.WithTimeoutCause. The request ctx is cancelled when the handler returns, so the legacy write is aborted, and the error is only recorded as a metric and never logged. The same pattern appears in Create, Delete, Update and DeleteCollection. The fix is to use context.WithoutCancel and to log the error.

answer.reasoning: All three suggestions point at lines 50-57 (Create) and report the same problem: the goroutine's context comes from the request context, so the legacy write is cancelled when the handler returns. They also all say the failure is silent because it is never logged. Each one names the same other sites (Delete 108-114, Update 134-141, DeleteCollection 161-167) and gives the same fix: context.WithoutCancel plus logging the error. Because every member already covers all four places and the logging issue, posting any one of them would fully replace the others. So the group is same_location and needs no unified comment. The judges agreed on the grouping and differed only on the kind and the unified-comment flag. Since every member already carries all the information, the systemic_pattern label with needsUnifiedComment=true is not needed here.
